items.text: You must be 19 or older to buy, possess or use non-medical cannabis. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public. Smoking or vaping is allowed outdoors where tobacco is, but not in parks (except designated areas and campsites), playgrounds, sports fields, skate parks, pools, public buildings, or within 6 m of their doors, windows and air intakes, and never in a vehicle or boat, even as a passenger.

laws.rule: The legal age for cannabis in British Columbia is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from government-operated stores in person and online or private licensed stores.

Smoking or vaping cannabis is generally allowed where tobacco smoking is, but not in parks (except some designated areas and campsites), at playgrounds, sports fields, skate parks and swimming pools, near schools, or within 6 metres of bus stops, transit shelters, train stations and ferry docks. Local bylaws may add limits.
Free day-use passes are required at Joffre Lakes, Garibaldi and Golden Ears in summer and Mount Seymour in winter; book online.
laws.heading: Day-use passes

laws.rule: Gwaii Haanas: everyone 17 and over must complete the orientation and score 80% on the quiz, and carry the booking receipt and certificate. Fees: daily C$29 (about A$29.48 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) adult, C$24.50 senior; seasonal C$171.50 adult, C$143 senior; youth 17 and under free.
laws.heading: Gwaii Haanas

laws.rule: Vancouver's Park Board runs an alcohol-on-beaches pilot. For 2026 the City said adults aged 19 and over could bring and drink alcohol, from the May long weekend to 30 September and between 11 am and 9 pm, at Jericho, Spanish Banks, Locarno, Second Beach, Kitsilano and John Hendry (Trout Lake) beaches. Drinking is not allowed at English Bay, Sunset or Third Beach. Glass containers are banned in parks and beaches. Separately, the Alcohol in Parks program allows drinking in listed parks (31 year-round sites in a 2023 release, with more added for summer), generally not in playgrounds, sports fields, off-leash dog areas or car parks. Check vancouver.ca/alcohol-in-parks for the current list.

local-law.note: BC Parks day-use passes added 5 November 2026; check the page for season dates. Gwaii Haanas added.

layers.process: Free day-use passes, booked online two days ahead from 7 am Pacific (not by phone). Joffre Lakes (Pipi7iyekw): required 11 May to 25 Oct 2026, each person needs one, up to four trail passes per transaction per day, 12 and under exempt with a pass-holding adult, park capped at 500 visitors a day. Garibaldi vehicle passes: Diamond Head and Rubble Creek Friday to Monday and holidays 12 Jun to 12 Oct; Cheakamus Lake daily 13 Jun to 7 Sep, then Friday to Monday and holidays to 12 Oct, with AM or PM slots. One pass per vehicle (up to 12 people). Camping reservation holders need no day pass.

layers.authority: Parks Canada, Pacific Rim National Park Reserve
layers.process: West Coast Trail: every hiker needs a Backcountry Use Permit; overnight hiking 1 May to 30 Sep, trail closed 7 Oct to 30 Apr. Daily quota; all spaces reservable (no standby). 2026 reservations opened 8 am PT on 5 Feb 2026 at reservation.pc.gc.ca or 1-877-737-3783. Max group 10. Permits not issued under age 6. Reservation, permit, orientation and ferry fees apply (amounts not on the page; see the fee schedule). Cancel 21 or more days ahead for refunds of permit, orientation and ferry fees.

Lake O'Hara: the day-use bus is allocated by random draw (applications 2 to 23 March 2026); shuttle runs 19 Jun to 4 Oct 2026, up to 6 people per reservation. Campground (30 sites, open 19 Jun to 4 Oct) booked from 10 Feb 2026; tent required, max 3 nights. Fees not listed on the page.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Indigenous Tourism BC (an Indigenous-led tourism body) says visitors are guests. Communities guide local protocol: research their guidelines and respect any request to stay away, especially in remote areas such as Haida Gwaii. Follow local advice, avoid unknown backcountry, and deal with wildlife only under local guides' direction.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Hidden spots may be sacred sites or traditional fishing areas. The page gives no site-by-site rules.
culture-and-protocol.photography_and_story_permissions: Not set out on the page. It advises speaking directly with tourism operators before travel.
culture-and-protocol.reciprocity_and_gifts: It suggests choosing Indigenous-owned lodging, meals and tours where possible, and staying longer in one area.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Each First Nation for its own territory; Indigenous Tourism BC lists operators (see its Authentic Indigenous designation).
culture-and-protocol.note: Province-wide guidance only; each Nation's own protocol applies and the Nations are not listed one by one here.
